content: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, marketed under the brand name VIREAD, is a prodrug of tenofovir. It is chemically classified as the fumaric acid salt of the bis-isopropyloxycarbonyloxymethyl ester derivative of tenofovir. Once administered, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate is metabolized in vivo to tenofovir, which is an acyclic nucleotide analog of adenosine 5'-monophosphate. This compound exhibits antiviral activity by targeting HIV-1 reverse transcriptase. The chemical name of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate is 9-[2-(phosphonomethoxy)propyl]adenine fumarate (1:1). It has a solubility of 52.4 mg/mL in distilled water at 25°C. VIREAD is available in two formulations: tablets and oral powder. VIREAD tablets are intended for oral administration and are available in strengths of 150 mg, 200 mg, 250 mg, and 300 mg of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. These doses correspond to 123 mg, 163 mg, 204 mg, and 245 mg of tenofovir disoproxil, respectively. Each tablet contains the following inactive ingredients: croscarmellose sodium, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, and pregelatinized starch. The 300 mg tablets are coated with Opadry II Y-30-10671-A, which includes FD&C Blue 2 aluminum lake, hypromellose 2910, lactose monohydrate, titanium dioxide, and triacetin. The 150 mg, 200 mg, and 250 mg tablets are coated with Opadry II 32K-18425, which contains hypromellose 2910, lactose monohydrate, titanium dioxide, and triacetin. VIREAD oral powder is also available for oral administration. It consists of white, taste-masked, coated granules containing 40 mg of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate per gram of powder, equivalent to 33 mg of tenofovir disoproxil. The oral powder formulation includes the following inactive ingredients: mannitol, hydroxypropyl cellulose, ethyl cellulose, and silicon dioxide.
